paragraphs: BlackRock, Inc. (together, with its subsidiaries, unless the context otherwise indicates, "BlackRock" or the "Company") is a leading publicly traded investment management firm with $14.0 trillion of assets under management ("AUM") at December 31, 2025. With approximately 24,900 employees in more than 30 countries who serve clients in over 100 countries across the globe, BlackRock provides a broad range of investment management and technology and subscription services to institutional and retail clients worldwide. On July 1, 2025, BlackRock completed the acquisition of 100% of the business and assets of HPS Investment Partners (the "HPS Transaction" or "HPS"), a leading global credit investment manager, with substantially all consideration paid in Class B-2 common units ("Subco Units") of BlackRock Saturn Subco, LLC ("Subco"), a consolidated subsidiary of the Company. Concurrent with the acquisition, BlackRock Finance, Inc., Global Infrastructure Management, LLC ("GIP"), HPS, and their respective subsidiaries became wholly owned subsidiaries of Subco. For additional information on the HPS Transaction see Note 3, Acquisitions, in the notes to the consolidated financial statements contained in Part II, Item 8 for additional information.

BlackRock's diverse platform of alpha-seeking active, private markets, index and cash management investment strategies across asset classes enables the Company to offer choice and tailor investment and asset allocation solutions for clients. Product offerings include single- and multi-asset portfolios investing in equities, fixed income, private markets, liquid alternatives, digital assets, currencies and commodities, and money market instruments. Products are offered directly and through intermediaries in a variety of vehicles, including open-end and closed-end mutual funds, iShares® exchange-traded funds ("ETFs"), separate accounts, collective trust funds and other pooled investment vehicles. BlackRock also offers technology and subscription services, including the investment and risk management technology platform, Aladdin®, Aladdin WealthTM, eFront®, Preqin, and Cachematrix®, as well as advisory services and solutions to a broad base of institutional and wealth management clients. The Company is highly regulated and manages its clients' assets as a fiduciary. The Company does not engage in proprietary trading activities that could conflict with the interests of its clients.

BlackRock serves a diverse mix of institutional and retail clients across the globe. Clients include tax-exempt institutions, such as defined benefit and defined contribution pension plans, charities, foundations and endowments; official institutions, such as central banks, sovereign wealth funds, supranationals and other government entities; taxable institutions, including insurance companies, financial institutions, corporations and third-party fund sponsors, and retail intermediaries.

BlackRock maintains a significant global sales and marketing presence that is focused on establishing and maintaining retail and institutional investment management and technology service relationships by marketing its services to investors directly and through third-party distribution relationships, including financial professionals and pension consultants.
BlackRock is an independent, publicly traded company, with no single majority shareholder and over 80% of its Board of Directors consisting of independent directors.
Management seeks to deliver value for stockholders over time by, among other things, capitalizing on BlackRock's differentiated competitive position, including:

• the Company's longstanding model of client choice, through which it offers a wide range of index, active, private markets, and whole portfolio solutions across broad markets, themes, regions, and investment styles;

• the Company's focus on strong investment performance, seeking the best risk-adjusted returns for client portfolios, within the mandates given by clients, to help them meet their investment objectives;

• the Company's research, data and analytics, which are at the center of BlackRock's investment approach and processes. They inform BlackRock's pursuit of the best risk-adjusted returns, and underpin product creation and innovation;

• the Company's global reach and commitment to best practices around the world, with approximately 60% of employees outside the United States ("US") serving clients locally and supporting local investment capabilities. Approximately 35% of total AUM is managed for clients domiciled outside the US;

• the Company's differentiated client relationships and fiduciary focus, which enable effective positioning toward changing client needs and industry trends including the secular shift to ETFs; growing allocations to private markets, such as infrastructure and private credit; increasing demand for outsourcing and whole portfolio solutions using index, active and private markets products; anticipated reallocations to fixed income; demand for high-performing active strategies; interest in sustainable investment strategies; and a continued focus on income and retirement; and

• the Company's longstanding commitment to innovation, technology services and the continued development of, and increased interest in, BlackRock technology products and solutions, including Aladdin, Aladdin Wealth, eFront, Preqin, and Cachematrix. This commitment is further extended by minority investments in financial technology and digital distribution providers, data and whole portfolio capabilities including Viridium, Generation Life, Securitize, Upvest, Avaloq, Human Interest, Circle, Clarity AI, Envestnet, Acorns, Scalable Capital and iCapital.
BlackRock operates in a global marketplace impacted by changing market dynamics and economic uncertainty, factors that can significantly affect earnings and stockholder returns in any given period.

The Company's ability to increase revenue, earnings and stockholder value over time is predicated on its ability to generate new business, including business in Aladdin and other technology products and services. New business efforts depend on BlackRock's ability to achieve clients' investment objectives, in a manner consistent with their risk preferences, to deliver excellent client service and to innovate in technology to serve clients' evolving needs. All of these efforts require the commitment and contributions of BlackRock employees. Accordingly, the ability to attract, develop and retain qualified professionals is critical to the Company's long-term success.

headings: Changes in interest or foreign exchange rates and/or global markets may impact BlackRock's AUM, base fees as well as net income and operating cash flows.

BlackRock's investment advisory contracts may be terminated or may not be renewed by clients and fund boards on favorable terms and the liquidation of certain funds may be accelerated at the option of investors.
The failure or negative performance of products offered by competitors may cause AUM in similar BlackRock products to decline irrespective of BlackRock's performance.
Increased competition may cause BlackRock's AUM, revenue and earnings to decline.
Failure to maintain Aladdin's competitive position in a dynamic market could lead to a loss of clients and could impede BlackRock's productivity and growth.
BlackRock may be unable to develop new products and services and the development of new products and services may expose BlackRock to reputational harm, additional costs or operational risk.
Changes in the value of seed and co-investments that BlackRock owns could affect its income and could increase the volatility of its earnings.
BlackRock indemnifies certain securities lending clients for specified losses as a result of a borrower default.
BlackRock's decision on whether to provide support to particular investment products from time to time, or the inability to provide support, may cause AUM, revenue and earnings to decline.
Climate-related risks could adversely affect BlackRock's business, products, operations and clients, which may cause BlackRock's AUM, revenue and earnings to decline.
Poor investment performance could lead to the loss of clients and may cause AUM, revenue and earnings to decline.
Performance fees may increase volatility of both revenue and earnings.
Failure to identify errors in the quantitative models BlackRock utilizes to manage its business could adversely affect product performance and client relationships.

Failure or unavailability of third-party dependencies may adversely affect Aladdin operations, which could cause reputational harm, lead to a loss of clients and impede BlackRock's productivity and growth.
A failure to effectively manage the development and use of AI, combined with an evolving regulatory environment, could have an adverse effect on BlackRock's growth, reputation or business.
Failure to maintain adequate corporate and contingent liquidity may cause BlackRock's AUM, liquidity and earnings to decline, as well as harm its prospects for growth.
Operating risks associated with BlackRock's securities lending program may result in client losses.
Inorganic transactions may harm the Company's competitive or financial position if they are not successful.
BlackRock is subject to risks associated with its recent acquisitions, including any failure to realize anticipated benefits of such acquisitions.
Operating in international markets increases BlackRock's operational, political, regulatory and other risks.

Fraud, the circumvention of controls or the violation of risk management and workplace policies could have an adverse effect on BlackRock's reputation, which may cause the Company's AUM, revenue and earnings to decline.
The failure to recruit, train and retain employees and develop and implement effective executive succession could lead to the loss of clients and may cause AUM, revenue and earnings to decline.
The impairment or failure of third parties may negatively impact the performance of products and accounts that BlackRock manages, which may cause BlackRock's AUM, revenue and earnings to decline.

paragraphs: As a global investment management firm, risk is an inherent part of BlackRock's business. Global markets, by their nature, are prone to uncertainty and subject participants to a variety of risks. While BlackRock devotes significant resources across all of its operations to identify, measure, monitor, manage and analyze market, operating, legal, compliance, reputational, fiduciary and investment risks, BlackRock's business, financial condition, operating results and nonoperating results could be materially adversely affected and the Company's stock price could decline as a result of any of these risks and uncertainties, including the ones discussed below.

Changes in the value levels of equity, debt, real assets, commodities, foreign exchange or other asset markets, including from the impact of global trade policies and tariffs, may cause assets under management ("AUM"), revenue and earnings to decline.

BlackRock's investment management revenue is primarily comprised of fees based on a percentage of the value of AUM and, in some cases, performance fees which are normally expressed as a percentage of returns to the client. Numerous factors, including price movements in the equity, debt or currency markets, or movements in the price of real assets, commodities, digital assets or other alternative investments in which BlackRock invests on behalf of its clients, including from the impact of global fiscal, monetary and trade policies, could cause:
• the value of AUM, or BlackRock's returns on AUM, to decrease; • client redemptions from BlackRock's products;
• client rebalancing or reallocating of assets into BlackRock products that yield lower fees;
• an impairment to the value of intangible assets and goodwill; or

paragraphs: BlackRock's strategy continues to be guided by the Company's clients' needs and focus on the long-term, which the Company believes better enables it to deliver durable returns for shareholders and create value for all of its stakeholders. BlackRock's highly diversified multi-product platform was created to meet client needs in all market environments and provide clients with choice in how they seek to achieve their unique financial goals. BlackRock is positioned to provide alpha-seeking active, private markets, index, and cash management investment strategies across asset classes and geographies. In addition, BlackRock leverages its world-class risk management, analytics, and technology capabilities, including the Aladdin platform, on behalf of clients. BlackRock serves a diverse mix of institutional and retail clients across the globe, as well as investors in ETFs, maintaining differentiated client relationships and a fiduciary focus. The diversity of BlackRock's platform facilitates the generation of organic growth in various market environments, and as client preferences evolve. BlackRock's long-term strategy remains to keep alpha at the heart of BlackRock; drive growth in ETFs, private markets, and technology; be the global leader in sustainable investing; and lead as a whole portfolio advisor.

BlackRock's framework for long-term shareholder value creation is predicated on generating differentiated organic growth, leveraging scale to increase operating margins over time, and returning capital to shareholders on a consistent basis. BlackRock's diversified platform, in terms of style, product, client, and geography, enables it to generate more stable cash flows through market cycles, positioning BlackRock to invest for the long-term by striking an appropriate balance between investing for future growth and prudent discretionary expense management.

BlackRock has invested to serve the full breadth of client needs. Clients increasingly want to build portfolios that are seamlessly integrated across public and private markets, and that are underpinned by data, risk management, and technology. The Company is differentiated in being able to deliver across public and private markets, equity and debt, and in the way that best serves each client – from broad-based ETFs to customized whole portfolio solutions. The Company also offers its Aladdin technology to support integrated public-private portfolios.

2025 was a milestone year of organic client activity and integration of acquisitions grounded in client needs, investment capability expansion, technology and scale. Clients awarded BlackRock with a record $698 billion of net inflows in 2025, driving 9% organic base fee growth. Technology services and subscription annual contract value ("ACV") grew 16% organically, reflecting both new and expanded client relationships. The Company's closing of the HPS and Preqin Transactions are expected to expand and enhance private markets investment and data capabilities.

BlackRock expects 2026 to be a dynamic investing environment. Mega forces like artificial intelligence ("AI"), financial technology innovation, and an ongoing evolution in debt financing are transforming economies and their long-term growth trajectories. Capital markets will play a key role in these transformations. Private markets assets are an increasingly vital part of capital markets, and blending both public and private markets will be critical in fully capturing growth opportunities.

BlackRock is well-positioned to capitalize on structural growth opportunities against a backdrop of economic and capital markets evolution. The Company has made coordinated investments to build the premier long-term capital partner and technology provider across public and private markets. The 2024 acquisition of GIP and the 2025 acquisitions of Preqin and HPS each better positioned BlackRock's platform ahead of evolving client needs and structural industry trends.

As the asset management landscape shifts globally from individual product selection to a whole-portfolio approach, BlackRock's strategy is focused on creating outcome-oriented client solutions for both retail investors and institutions. This includes having a diverse platform of alpha-seeking active, index and private markets products, as well as enhanced distribution and portfolio construction technology offerings. Digital wealth tools are an important component of BlackRock's retail strategy, as BlackRock scales and customizes model portfolios, extends Aladdin Wealth and digital wealth partnerships globally, and helps advisors build better portfolios through portfolio construction and risk management, powered by Aladdin. BlackRock has also seen strong momentum in outsourcing solutions among wealth and institutional clients, including the funding of several significant mandates in 2026, and anticipates continued outsourcing opportunities in the future.

BlackRock has built a broad private markets platform with $323 billion of AUM across infrastructure, private credit, real estate, private equity and multi-alternatives. As of December 31, 2025, BlackRock had approximately $91 billion of committed capital to deploy for clients in a variety of private markets strategies, and remains confident in its ability to accelerate growth as a leader in private markets. BlackRock also manages $101 billion in liquid alternatives, as well as $105 billion in liquid credit strategies, included within fixed income AUM. BlackRock's alternatives platform totals approximately $676 billion in client assets, making it a top five alternatives provider.

BlackRock's investments in infrastructure, private credit, and alternatives-to-wealth underpin its ambition to raise $400 billion in private markets by 2030. The Company has a significant opportunity to deliver better outcomes and experiences for clients in their private markets allocations. For example, BlackRock is the largest general account manager for insurers with $720 billion in long-term AUM. With HPS, it's now also one of the largest asset-based finance and high-grade managers. The Company is focused on helping insurers build more dynamic and diversified portfolios across public and private markets, which could contribute to organic AUM and base fee growth.

Similarly in wealth, BlackRock is working to expand access to private markets. The Company is bringing together investment performance track records with its scaled global distribution model. BlackRock plans to continue to expand and diversify distribution of HPS' nontraded business development companies to US wirehouses and registered investment advisors. It also plans to widen its product range through an H-Series family of funds in 2026. The Company aims to bring together the building blocks to serve wealth investors through a coordinated, multi-alternatives portfolio.

For retirement savers, the Company also sees opportunity to bring additional returns and diversification to investors through private markets. BlackRock is well positioned to build on its position as an innovator and leader in retirement, notably through its LifePath target date franchise, which includes LifePath Paycheck. BlackRock has a leading defined contribution investment only ("DCIO") platform, a $600 billion LifePath franchise, a top five alternatives platform and Preqin. The Company expects to launch its first LifePath target date fund with private markets in 2026.

The private markets – and clients' allocations to them – are expected to continue to grow. Standardized, transparent private markets data and analytics will be increasingly important. As with Aladdin, BlackRock believes it can add even more value to Preqin as both a user and provider of private markets data and risk analytics. Aladdin expanded into new asset classes and markets as BlackRock and its clients evolved, and it expects the same for Preqin.

In addition to private markets, BlackRock is executing on a strong opportunity set across multiple growth channels. These include ETFs, whole portfolio solutions like outsourced mandates and models, systematic active strategies, fixed income, and technology.

The ETF industry has been growing rapidly, driven by structural tailwinds including the use of ETFs as active tools, the migration from commission-based to fee-based wealth management, growth in model portfolios, expansion of digital wealth platforms, and the modernization of the bond market. BlackRock's ETF growth strategy is centered on increasing scale and pursuing global growth themes in client and product channels, including Core Equity, Fixed Income, Digital Assets, Active, and Precision ETFs. BlackRock views ETFs as a technology that facilitates investing, and ETFs have become core to asset management. The Company believes that ETFs will continue to be a structural growth area as clients turn to ETFs as the preferred vehicle for investing strategies of all types. BlackRock has been a leader in expanding the market for ETFs by making them more accessible and by delivering new asset classes like bonds or digital assets and investment strategies like active. Approximately a quarter of 2025 ETF net inflows of $527 billion were into products launched in the last five years. Active ETFs delivered $54 billion in net inflows in 2025, and BlackRock's US equity factor rotation active ETF was the highest grossing active ETF in the industry. BlackRock fixed income ETFs generated a record $159 billion of net inflows, and the Company had both the highest net inflowing active and index fixed income ETFs in the industry. BlackRock will continue to innovate at the product and portfolio level and accelerate distribution capabilities to deliver differentiated investment solutions.

BlackRock, Inc. (together, with its subsidiaries, unless the context otherwise indicates, "BlackRock" or the "Company") 是一家領先的上市公司投資管理公司，截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，其管理資產規模 ("AUM") 約為 14.0 兆美元。擁有約 24,900 名員工，分佈於超過 30 個國家，服務全球超過 100 個國家的客戶，BlackRock 提供廣泛的投資管理及科技與訂閱服務，服務全球機構與零售客戶。2025 年 7 月 1 日，BlackRock 完成收購 HPS Investment Partners (the "HPS Transaction" or "HPS")，一家領先的全球信貸投資管理公司，取得其 100% 的業務與資產，交易中約有 substantially all 的對價以 BlackRock Saturn Subco, LLC ("Subco") 的 Class B-2 普通單位 ("Subco Units") 支付，Subco 為本公司之合併子公司。同時，BlackRock Finance, Inc., Global Infrastructure Management, LLC ("GIP"), HPS 及其各自子公司成為 Subco 的 wholly owned 子公司。有關 HPS 交易之更多資訊，請參閱財務報表附註第 3 項，即「收購」，內容包含於 Part II, Item 8 之合併財務報表附註中。

BlackRock 跨不同資產類別提供追求 alpha 的主動投資、私有市場、指數及現金管理投資策略，使本公司能為客戶提供選擇性與客製化的投資與資產配置解決方案。產品包括投資於股票、固定收益、私有市場、流動替代投資、數位資產、貨幣與商品，以及貨幣市場工具之單一與多資產組合。產品直接提供，並透過中介機構以多種投資工具提供，包括開放式與封閉式共同基金、iShares® 交易所交易基金 ("ETFs"), 分離帳戶、集體信託基金及其他集資投資工具。BlackRock 亦提供科技與訂閱服務，包括投資與風險管理科技平台 Aladdin®, Aladdin WealthTM, eFront®, Preqin, 和 Cachematrix®, 以及針對廣泛機構與資產管理客戶的諮詢服務與解決方案。本公司受高度監管，並以信託人身份管理客戶資產。本公司不從事可能與客戶利益衝突的 proprietary 交易活動。
BlackRock 服務全球多樣化的機構與零售客戶。客戶包括免稅機構，如確定給付與確定提繳退休金計畫、慈善機構、基金會與捐助財團；官方機構，如中央銀行、主權財富基金、超國家機構及其他政府機構；課稅機構，包括保險公司、金融機構、公司與第三方基金發起人，以及零售中介機構。
BlackRock 保持著重要的全球銷售與行銷據點，專注於建立與維持零售與機構投資管理與科技服務關係，透過直接行銷服務至投資人，以及透過第三方分銷關係，包括金融專業人士與退休金顧問。
BlackRock 是一家獨立上市公司，無單一主要股東，且董事會超過 80% 為獨立董事。
管理階層致力於長遠為股東創造價值，包括利用 BlackRock 的差異化競爭優勢，例如：
• 本公司長期的客戶選擇模式，透過該模式，本公司提供廣泛的指數、主動、私有市場與整體投資組合解決方案，涵蓋廣泛市場、主題、地區與投資風格；
• 本公司重視強勁的投資績效，追求符合客戶投資授權下最佳風險調整後回報，協助客戶達成其投資目標；
• 本公司之研究、數據與分析，為貝萊德投資方法與流程之核心。這些內容協助貝萊德追求最佳風險調整後回報，並作為產品開發與創新之基礎。
• 本公司之全球佈局與對全球最佳實踐之承諾，約有 60% 員工位於美國（"US"）以外地區，為客戶提供本地化服務，並支援當地投資能力。約有 35% 的總管理資產規模（AUM）為服務位於美國以外地區之客戶所管理。
• 本公司之獨特客戶關係與受託責任，使其能有效應對客戶需求與產業趨勢之變化，包括長期向 ETF 轉型；對私人市場（如基礎建設與私人信貸）之投資配置增加；對委外服務與整體投資組合解決方案之需求增加，使用指數、主動與私人市場產品；預期對固定收益之重新配置；對高績效主動策略之需求；對永續投資策略之興趣；以及持續關注收入與退休規劃。

• 本公司長久以來對創新、科技服務及持續發展與增加興趣於貝萊德科技產品與解決方案之承諾，包括 Aladdin、Aladdin Wealth、eFront、Preqin 及 Cachematrix。此承諾進一步延伸至對金融科技與數位分銷提供者、數據與整體投資組合能力之少數投資，包括 Viridium、Generation Life、Securitize、Upvest、Avaloq、Human Interest、Circle、Clarity AI、Envestnet、Acorns、Scalable Capital 及 iCapital。
貝萊德營運於受市場動態變化與經濟不確定性影響之全球市場，這些因素可能在任何特定期間顯著影響營收與股東回報。
本公司能於長遠時間內提高營收、獲利與股東價值之能力，取決於其能創造新業務，包括 Aladdin 及其他科技產品與服務之業務。新業務努力取決於貝萊德能以符合客戶風險偏好的方式達成投資目標，提供優質客戶服務，並透過科技創新以應對客戶不斷變化的需求。所有這些努力皆需要貝萊德員工之承諾與貢獻。因此，吸引、培養與留住合適專業人才對本公司之長遠成功至關重要。

paragraphs: BlackRock 的策略持續以本公司客戶的需要為導向，並聚焦於長遠，本公司認為這有助於更有效地為股東創造可持續的回報，並為所有利害關係人創造價值。BlackRock 的高度分散化多產品平台是為應對所有市場環境中客戶的需求，並提供客戶選擇如何達成其獨特財務目標的方式。BlackRock 有能力在各資產類別與地理區域提供追求 Alpha 的主動投資、私人市場、指數與現金管理投資策略。此外，BlackRock 藉助其世界級的風險管理、分析與科技能力，包括 Aladdin 平台，為客戶提供服務。BlackRock 服務全球多樣化的機構與零售客戶，以及 ETF 投資者，維持差異化的客戶關係與受託責任。BlackRock 平台的多樣性有助於在各種市場環境中產生內生性成長，並隨著客戶偏好變化而調整。BlackRock 的長遠策略仍是以 Alpha 為核心；推動 ETF、私人市場與科技的成長；成為永續投資的全球領導者；並作為整體投資組合顧問領導者。
BlackRock 創造長期股東價值的架構建立在產生差異化的內生性成長、利用規模提高營運毛利率，並定期回饋資本給股東的基礎之上。BlackRock 多元化的平台，從風格、產品、客戶與地理區域而言，使其能透過市場週期產生更穩定的現金流，使 BlackRock 能夠以適當的平衡投資於未來成長與謹慎的酌情支出管理，來進行長期投資。
BlackRock 已投資以服務客戶的全方位需求。客戶日益希望建立整合公共與私人市場的投資組合，並以數據、風險管理與科技為基礎。本公司能提供公共與私人市場、股權與債務的全方位服務，並以最符合每個客戶需求的方式進行，從廣泛的 ETF 到客製化的整體投資組合解決方案。本公司也提供 Aladdin 科技以支持整合的公共與私人市場投資組合。
2025 年是本公司以客戶需求為基礎，進行內生性客戶活動及收購整合的重要里程碑年，並基於投資能力擴張、技術與規模。客戶於 2025 年授予本公司創紀錄的 698 十億美元淨流入，推動 9% 內生性基本費用成長。技術服務與訂閱年度合約價值（"ACV"）以內生性成長 16%，反映新客戶關係與擴展的客戶關係。本公司完成 HPS 與 Preqin 交易後，預期將擴大並強化私募市場投資與數據能力。
BlackRock 預期 2026 年將是投資環境的動態年。巨觀力量如人工智慧（"AI"）、金融科技創新，以及債務融資的持續演進，正在改變經濟與其長期成長路徑。資本市場將在這些轉變中扮演關鍵角色。私人市場資產正成為資本市場越來越重要的組成部分，並融合公共與私人市場將是充分把握成長機會的關鍵。
BlackRock 在經濟與資本市場演進的背景下，處於有利位置以把握結構性成長機會。本公司已進行協調投資，以建立在公共與私人市場中首屈一指的長期資本夥伴與科技供應商。2024 年收購 GIP 與 2025 年收購 Preqin 與 HPS，皆使 BlackRock 的平台更符合演變中的客戶需求與結構性產業趨勢。

隨著全球資產管理領域從個別產品選擇轉向整體投資組合方法，BlackRock 的策略聚焦於為零售投資者與機構創造以結果為導向的客戶解決方案。這包括擁有多樣化的追求 Alpha 的主動投資、指數與私人市場產品，以及增強的分銷與投資組合構建科技服務。數位財富工具是 BlackRock 零售策略的重要組成部分，因為 BlackRock 正擴展與客製化模型投資組合，拓展 Aladdin 財富與數位財富合作夥伴全球，並協助顧問透過投資組合構建與風險管理，以 Aladdin 為動力，建立更好的投資組合。BlackRock 也觀察到在財富與機構客戶中對委外解決方案的強勁動能，包括在 2026 年籌資數個重要的委外業務，並預期未來持續有委外機會。

BlackRock 已建立廣泛的私募市場平台，管理資產規模達 323 十億美元，涵蓋基礎建設、私募信貸、不動產、私募股權與多類型替代投資。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，BlackRock 約有 91 十億美元的承諾資本可用於客戶的多種私募市場策略，並對其作為私募市場領導者加速成長的能力保持信心。BlackRock 運作管理 101 十億美元的流動性替代投資，以及 105 十億美元的流動性信貸策略，包含於固定收益 AUM 內。BlackRock 的替代投資平台總管理資產規模約為 676 十億美元，使其成為前五大替代投資服務商。

BlackRock 的投資於基礎建設、私人信貸及替代性資產，奠定了其在 2030 年前於私人市場籌集 4000 億美元的願景。本公司有機會在私人市場配置中為客戶帶來更好的成果與體驗。例如，BlackRock 是保險公司最大的一般帳戶管理人，管理資產規模達 7200 億美元。透過 HPS，它現在也是最大的以資產為基礎的融資及高級資產管理人之一。本公司專注於協助保險公司建立更動態且多元化的公共與私人市場投資組合，這可能有助於自有資產規模與基本費用的成長。
同樣在財富管理領域，BlackRock 正努力擴大私人市場的投資管道。本公司正將投資績效紀錄與其規模化的全球銷售模式結合。BlackRock 計畫持續擴大與多元化 HPS 非交易性業務發展公司的銷售管道至美國經紀商與註冊投資顧問。它也計畫透過 H-Series 系列基金於 2026 年擴展其產品範圍。本公司目標是透過協調的多類型投資組合，為財富管理投資者提供所需的投資組合元件。

對於退休儲蓄者，本公司也看到透過私人市場為投資者帶來額外報酬與分散風險的機會。BlackRock 有條件在退休領域中成為創新者與領導者，特別是透過其 LifePath 目標日期品牌，包括 LifePath Paycheck。BlackRock 擁有領先的僅限於退休計畫投資（"DCIO"）平台，一個 6000 億美元的 LifePath 品牌，一個前五大替代性資產平台與 Preqin。本公司預期於 2026 年推出首款包含私人市場的 LifePath 目標日期基金。
私人市場 – 以及客戶對其的配置 – 預期會持續成長。標準化、透明的私人市場數據與分析將變得越來越重要。如同 Aladdin，BlackRock 相信其可以作為私人市場數據與風險分析的使用者與提供者，為 Preqin 增加更多價值。Aladdin 隨著 BlackRock 及其客戶的發展，擴展至新的資產類別與市場，BlackRock 也預期 Preqin 會有相同的發展。
除了私人市場，BlackRock 正在多個成長管道中執行強大的機會組合。這些包括 ETFs、整體投資組合解決方案如委外投資指標與模型、系統化主動策略、固定收益與科技。

ETF 行業正在快速成長，受到結構性風向的驅動，包括將 ETF 用作主動工具、從佣金制轉為費用制的財富管理、模型投資組合的成長、數位財富平台的擴張以及債券市場的現代化。BlackRock 的 ETF 成長策略以增加規模與追求客戶與產品管道中的全球成長主題為中心，包括核心股票、固定收益、數位資產、主動策略與精準 ETFs。BlackRock 將 ETF 觀視為一種促進投資的科技，ETF 已成為資產管理的核心。本公司相信 ETF 將持續成為結構性成長領域，因為客戶轉向 ETF 作為所有類型投資策略的首選工具。BlackRock 已經在擴大 ETF 市場中扮演領導角色，透過使其更易於取得，並提供如債券或數位資產的新資產類別與主動投資策略。2025 年 ETF 的淨流入約 5270 億美元中，有四分之一流入的是過去五年內推出的產品。主動 ETF 在 2025 年實現了 540 億美元的淨流入，而 BlackRock 的美國股票因子輪動主動 ETF 是業界最高的主動 ETF。BlackRock 的固定收益 ETF 產生了創紀錄的 1590 億美元淨流入，本公司同時擁有業界最高的主動與指數固定收益 ETF 的淨流入。BlackRock 將持續在產品與投資組合層面創新，並加速分銷能力，以提供差異化的投資解決方案。

headings: 利率或外匯匯率及/或全球市場的變動可能影響 BlackRock 的管理資產規模、基本費用以及淨收入與營運現金流。
BlackRock 的投資顧問契約可能被客戶及基金董事會終止或不以有利條款續約，且投資者可能選擇加速某些基金的清算。
競爭對手所提供產品的失敗或表現不佳，可能導致類似 BlackRock 產品的管理資產規模下降，與 BlackRock 的表現無關。
競爭增加可能導致 BlackRock 的管理資產規模、營業收入及獲利下降。
未能維持 Aladdin 在動態市場中的競爭地位，可能導致客戶流失，並可能影響 BlackRock 的生產力與成長。
BlackRock 可能無法開發新產品與服務，且新產品與服務的開發可能使 BlackRock 面臨聲譽損害、額外成本或營運風險。
BlackRock 所擁有種子投資及共同投資的價值變動，可能影響其收入，並可能增加其獲利的波動性。
BlackRock 為某些證券借貸客戶就借款人違約所導致的特定損失提供賠償。
BlackRock 決定是否偶爾提供特定投資產品支援，或無法提供支援，可能導致 AUM、營業收入及獲利下降。
與氣候相關的風險可能對 BlackRock 的業務、產品、營運及客戶產生不利影響，可能導致 BlackRock 的 AUM、營業收入及獲利下降。
投資表現不佳可能導致客戶流失，並可能導致 AUM、營業收入及獲利下降。
績效費用可能增加營業收入及獲利的波動性。
未能識別 BlackRock 用以管理其業務的量化模型中的錯誤，可能對產品表現及客戶關係產生不利影響。
未能識別或第三方依賴項無法使用，可能對 Aladdin 營運產生不利影響，可能導致聲譽受損、客戶流失，並影響 BlackRock 的生產力與成長。
未能有效管理 AI 的開發與應用，加上不斷演進的監管環境，可能對 BlackRock 的成長、聲譽或業務產生不利影響。
未能維持充足的企業及應變流動性，可能導致 BlackRock 的 AUM、流動性及獲利下降，並損害其成長前景。
與 BlackRock 證券融資計劃相關的營運風險可能導致客戶損失。
非金屬交易若未成功，可能損害本公司的競爭地位或財務狀況。
BlackRock 面臨與其近期收購相關的風險，包括未能實現預期收購效益的風險。
在國際市場營運會增加 BlackRock 的營運、政治、法規及其他風險。
詐欺、繞過控制措施或違反風險管理及工作政策的情況，可能對 BlackRock 的聲譽產生負面影響，這可能會導致本公司的 AUM、營業收入及獲利下降。
未能招募、培訓及留住員工，以及未能有效發展及實施高階主管繼任計畫，可能導致客戶流失，並可能導致 AUM、營業收入及獲利下降。
第三方的虧損或失敗可能對 BlackRock 管理的產品及帳戶表現產生負面影響，這可能會導致 BlackRock 的 AUM、營業收入及獲利下降。
本公司分銷渠道的任何中斷可能導致 BlackRock 的 AUM、營業收入及獲利下降
paragraphs: 作為一家全球性投資管理公司，風險是 BlackRock 事業的一部分。全球市場本質上容易產生不確定性，並使參與者面臨多種風險。雖然 BlackRock 在所有運作中投入大量資源，用以識別、衡量、監測、管理及分析市場、營運、法律、合規、聲譽、信託及投資風險，但 BlackRock 的業務、財務狀況、營運結果及非營運結果可能受到這些風險與不確定性重大不利影響，而本公司股票價格也可能因此下跌，包括下列所討論的風險與不確定性。
股權、債務、實物資產、商品、外匯或其他資產市場的價值變動，包括全球貿易政策與關稅的影響，可能會導致受託管理資產（"AUM"）、營業收入及獲利下降。
BlackRock 的投資管理營業收入主要由基於受託管理資產價值百分比的費用組成，有時也會包含績效費用，通常以客戶回報的百分比表示。許多因素，包括股權、債務或貨幣市場的價格變動，或實物資產、商品、數位資產或其他替代投資品種的價格變動，包括全球財政、貨幣及貿易政策的影響，可能會導致：
• 本公司管理的資產規模（AUM）或對AUM的回報率下降；• 客戶從BlackRock產品中提領資金；
• 客戶重新配置資產至BlackRock產品，而該產品費用較低；
• 智慧財產權及商譽價值減損；
